title: Merge dialog lists only the first 50 accepted proposals as targets
body:
## Summary
MergeDialog loads merge targets with one inbox.list call and ignores its `next` cursor, so in an inbox with more than PAGE_SIZE accepted proposals the older ones cannot be found by ref or title.

## Description
forge/static/app/src/routes/inbox/dialogs.jsx:161-162 calls `inbox.list {project_key, status: 'accepted'}` once and flattens `groups`; `res.next` is dropped. The server pages at PAGE_SIZE = 50 (forge/src/core/types.mjs:41; forge/src/core/cards.mjs:236-239, :259 sets `next`). The search box (:172-173) filters only that loaded slice, and the empty text says 'No matching proposal.' (:214) although the proposal exists. Typing DW-n in the Jira-key field works (:178 accepts DW_REF_RE), but nothing tells the person that.

## Flow
- Inbox has 60 accepted proposals
- Open Merge on an open card, type the ref of the 55th accepted one
- Dialog says 'No matching proposal.'
- Person concludes it does not exist and accepts a duplicate instead

## Expected impact
Merging into the right existing item is the duplicate-control door; a silent miss produces duplicate Jira issues.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every accepted proposal is findable
Before: targets = first 50 accepted (one page)
After: search reaches all accepted (follow `next`, or a server-side text filter), or the empty text names the limit and points at the DW-n field
Method: simulation - walked 3 cases (10, 50, 60 accepted) through dialogs.jsx and cards.mjs paging; no populated store to probe
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/static/app/src/routes/inbox/dialogs.jsx:161 `call('inbox.list', { project_key: card.project_key, status: 'accepted' }).then(` :162 `(res) => { if (live) setAccepted((res.groups ?? []).flatMap((g) => g.items ?? [])); }` ; forge/src/core/types.mjs:41 `export const PAGE_SIZE = 50;` ; forge/src/core/cards.mjs:259 `next: rows.length > PAGE_SIZE ? String(offset + PAGE_SIZE) : undefined`
impact_why: Merge is the duplicate-control path; big inboxes silently lose older targets

title: Draft the fix posts a duplicate Confluence comment on every press after a reload
body:
## Summary
The byline's "Draft the fix as a comment" button forgets it already posted as soon as the byline remounts, and the server posts a fresh footer comment each call, so a page collects one identical Dowser comment per press.

## Description
DraftFix keeps 'done' only in component state (forge/static/app/src/routes/byline/index.jsx:55, :65). A reload of the page or of the byline popup shows the button again (:68-70). The resolver draftFix (forge/src/core/doc-drift.mjs:153-168) checks only that the page links the item (:157-158) and calls addFooterComment (:164) with no lookup of an earlier comment for the same page+ref, and byline.forPage returns no marker of a posted comment, so neither side can tell.

## Flow
- Open a Confluence page whose byline lists a Doc drift proposal
- Press Draft the fix: comment 1 posted, button replaced by the status line
- Reload the page, open the byline again: the button is back
- Press again: comment 2, identical, posted as the same person

## Expected impact
Prevents duplicate public comments on team pages (a visible artifact of the app) and makes the action idempotent per page+ref.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one comment per page+ref
Before: N presses across N byline mounts = N identical footer comments
After: second press answers the existing comment (or the byline shows 'Comment posted <date>' with a link) and posts nothing
Method: simulation - three cases walked through byline/index.jsx and doc-drift.mjs (first press, reload+press, two tabs); no Confluence to probe from a read-only scout
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
forge/static/app/src/routes/byline/index.jsx:55 `const [state, setState] = useState(... ({ s: 'idle' }));` :65 `if (state.s === 'done') return

Comment posted below the page...` ; forge/src/core/doc-drift.mjs:157 `const linked = await deps.db.query('SELECT 1 FROM page_links WHERE page_id = ? AND proposal_id = ?', ...)` :164 `made = await deps.confluence.addFooterComment(pageId, fixComment(card, ...))` - no query for an earlier comment id; :168 returns `{ comment: { page_id, id: made.id, ref } }` which nothing stores
impact_why: Duplicate comments posted as the person on shared docs; visible to every page reader

title: Remove the unused second HelpDialog and its drifting key list in dialogs.jsx
body:
## Summary
dialogs.jsx exports a HelpDialog with its own KEYS table that nothing imports; the live one is a private copy in InboxDialogs.jsx, and the two already say different things.

## Description
forge/static/app/src/routes/inbox/dialogs.jsx:277-299 defines KEYS and `export function HelpDialog`. The only consumers of dialogs.jsx import AcceptDialog, MergeDialog, RejectDialog (InboxDialogs.jsx:6) and SnoozeStep (InboxList.jsx:7, ReadingPane.jsx:4). InboxDialogs.jsx:17 renders its own HelpDialog (:60) with KEYS at :49-58. Wording has diverged: 'Select or unselect' vs 'Check or uncheck'; the dead copy lacks '1 to 6 picks the reason, Ctrl+Enter confirms'. An edit to the wrong copy changes nothing on screen.

## Flow
- Developer greps for the shortcut help text
- Finds dialogs.jsx:277 first (exported, named HelpDialog)
- Edits it; the shipped help is unchanged

## Expected impact
One source of truth for the shortcut list; about 23 dead lines gone.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - zero dead exports in the inbox route
Before: 2 HelpDialog definitions, 1 rendered
After: 1
Method: probe - grep over the repo for HelpDialog and dialogs.jsx imports (zero consumers of the export)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep -rn HelpDialog forge/static/app/src -> dialogs.jsx:288 `export function HelpDialog`, InboxDialogs.jsx:17 `<HelpDialog onClose={closeDialog} />`, InboxDialogs.jsx:60 `function HelpDialog`; imports of dialogs.jsx: InboxDialogs.jsx:6 `import { AcceptDialog, MergeDialog, RejectDialog } from './dialogs.jsx';` InboxList.jsx:7 / ReadingPane.jsx:4 `import { SnoozeStep } from './dialogs.jsx';` ; dialogs.jsx:279 `['x', 'Select or unselect the proposal']` vs InboxDialogs.jsx:51 `['x', 'Check or uncheck the proposal for a bulk action']`
impact_why: Prevents edits landing in a copy no one sees

title: Snooze help promises Enter, Ctrl+Enter does nothing there; reject says fixed 6 s
body:
## Summary
Two help strings state a rule the code does not hold: the shortcut help's snooze line and the Reject dialog's fixed '6 seconds'.

## Description
InboxDialogs.jsx:54 says snooze is 'Enter to confirm' - true only while focus is in a text or date input of the SnoozeStep form (dialogs.jsx:331-334); the Ctrl+Enter rule the help teaches for a and r (InboxDialogs.jsx:52-53) is handled only inside Dialog (ui.jsx:82-87) and the open-dialog listener (useInboxKeys.js:56-73, which returns when no dialog is open), and the snooze step is a form, not a Dialog. RejectDialog says 'You get 6 seconds to undo.' (dialogs.jsx:272) while the window pauses on hover/focus (Toast.jsx:17-18, useCommitWindow.js:74-80) and its length is a parameter (useCommitWindow.js:8, :18), so copy and constant can drift.

## Flow
- Person presses s, tabs to the Snooze button, presses Ctrl+Enter as the help taught for a/r: nothing happens
- Reject copy promises a fixed 6 s although the toast pauses

## Expected impact
Help text a keyboard user can trust; one source for the undo duration.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - help matches behaviour
Before: Ctrl+Enter ignored in the snooze step; '6 seconds' literal
After: snooze step accepts Ctrl+Enter like every dialog (or help says Enter only); reject copy built from COMMIT_MS
Method: simulation - three key sequences walked through useInboxKeys.js, ui.jsx Dialog onKeyDown and the SnoozeStep form; no browser in a read-only scout
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: forge/static/app/src/routes/inbox/InboxDialogs.jsx:54 `['s', 'Snooze, with an optional note and Until date, Enter to confirm ...']` ; :53 `['r', 'Reject ...; 1 to 6 picks the reason, Ctrl+Enter confirms']` ; dialogs.jsx:334 `onKeyDown={(e) => { if (e.key === 'Escape') { e.stopPropagation(); onCancel(); } }}` (no Ctrl+Enter) ; useInboxKeys.js:57 `if (!dialog) return undefined;` ; dialogs.jsx:272 `You get 6 seconds to undo.` ; useCommitWindow.js:8 `export const COMMIT_MS = 6000;`
impact_why: Keyboard-first triage is the inbox's core; help that is wrong costs trust
